subject: Interpreting 'service boundary' for ISO ↔ FedRAMP crosswalk — evidence duration question
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena@pegasusaudits.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Bank Security <sec-questions@acme-bank.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on service boundary for ISO-27001 / FedRAMP mapping

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As we start mapping ISO controls to the FedRAMP baseline for Acme Bank, a couple of scope questions came up that will affect the evidence we request:

1) "Service boundary" definition: for customers using Redwood Private (VPC) vs Redwood Dedicated, do you consider the customer VPC network and self-managed components (e.g., customer KMS for BYOK) outside your ISO control boundary, or is some of that in-scope because of how you manage agent-side collectors/agents?

2) Evidence retention: FedRAMP typically expects 12+ months of high-fidelity logs tied to access and changes. For ISO sampling we understand shorter windows are acceptable, but Acme has asked how you retain and present historical KV-cache access and low-level inference logs (request/response metadata) for escalations and audits. Is there a consolidated export format you provide?

If you can point us to a short note or confirm via reply, that will help us finalize the initial evidence ask. If preferable, happy to jump on a 30-min call Monday.

Thanks,
Lena Park
Senior Auditor, Pegasus Audits

(pegasus: attachment request template attached on our side)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@pegasusaudits.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Acme Bank Security <sec-questions@acme-bank.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on service boundary for ISO-27001 / FedRAMP mapping

Lena — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Olga and Mina to confirm technical boundaries and evidence retention specifics. Ben, can you confirm any changes to the customer contract language that affects whether we assert control vs customer ownership for the VPC bundle?

Quick provisional answers while Olga/Mina jump in:
- For Redwood Private (VPC) we treat the customer-managed VPC, customer-managed KMS, and their tenant accounts as out-of-scope for Redwood's ISO boundary. However, components we operate (the private control plane, the agents we deploy into the VPC for telemetry ingestion, and the dedicated inference runtime we manage) are in-scope.
- Evidence exports: we can provide a time-bounded export of access logs, agent heartbeats, and inference metadata (headers, timestamps, non-user PII redacted) for the last 12 months as a packaged CSV/ndjson. There are some practical limits on raw request/response bodies for privacy reasons.

I'll let Olga/Mina add technical nuance and attach a short draft of our control-mapping we can share with Acme.

—Grace
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachment: control-mapping-draft.xlsx

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lena Park <lena@pegasusaudits.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Acme Bank Security <sec-questions@acme-bank.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on service boundary for ISO-27001 / FedRAMP mapping

Hi all — adding a bit more detail on the technical boundary so the auditor can mark where we assert control vs customer responsibility:

- VPC & networking: The customer VPC, subnets, and customer-managed routing are out-of-scope. Redwood's agents that we install into the customer's VPC run as managed daemons in customer namespaces; we consider the agent binary and its configuration we manage (push updates, restart) as in-scope. Network traffic egress/ingress policy enforcement is typically customer-side (we provide recommended firewall rules).

- KMS/BYOK: If the customer supplies BYOK (their KMS keys), key lifecycle operations (rotate, encrypt/decrypt) are handled by the customer's KMS and are out-of-scope. We do maintain logs of our service's calls to the KMS (call metadata, not raw keys), which we include in evidence packages. If the customer requests Redwood-managed keys, those key lifecycle controls are in-scope for Redwood and we can show key rotation records and KMS audit trails.

- Inference logs vs telemetry: We maintain three artifacts: 1) operational telemetry (CPU/GPU metrics, agent heartbeats), 2) request metadata (timestamps, model used, token counts, request ID), and 3) customer-provided payloads. We redact customer payloads by default and do not retain raw user prompts beyond a short buffering window unless the customer enables retention for debugging (opt-in). For FedRAMP mapping we can provide (2) for 12 months and (1) for 24 months in aggregated form.

I will attach a short table in the control-mapping draft that explicitly marks "redwood-managed" vs "customer-managed" for each control.

—Olga
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Lena Park <lena@pegasusaudits.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Acme Bank Security <sec-questions@acme-bank.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on service boundary for ISO-27001 / FedRAMP mapping

Adding specifics on retention exports and format so Acme knows what to expect:

- Export format: request metadata and telemetry are exported as gzipped ndjson. Each line is a JSON object for a single event (request or metric). We provide a manifest with schema version and sampling notes.
- Retention windows: request metadata = 12 months full fidelity; agent heartbeats/metrics = 24 months aggregated (1-min resolution up to 90 days, hourly afterwards).
- Redaction: any field marked as user_content or prompt_text is excluded unless the customer has explicitly enabled retention and signed the data-processing addendum.
- Evidence we can provide for key lifecycle: key creation timestamp, rotation events, and KMS audit IDs (we cannot export customer-managed key material).

If Acme needs a formal attestation about what is in our control boundary for ISO-27001, we can produce a short signed statement (1 page) and include it in the package.

—Mina
Head of Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: evidence-retention-summary.pdf

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarification on service boundary for ISO-27001 / FedRAMP mapping

Lena / Acme team — thanks for the quick review and for the questions. Per Olga and Mina above, the practical rule is: customer-managed infra (VPC, customer KMS, tenant-managed secrets) = out-of-scope; Redwood-managed control plane and managed agents = in-scope. We will deliver the control-mapping draft and the retention summary today; please flag any controls you want us to expand with sample evidence.

Next steps:
- I propose a 30-min alignment call Tuesday 9/15 to walk through the mapping and decide the evidence sample set Acme will need for the initial FedRAMP intake. Lena — can you send 2 windows that work?
- Ben — please confirm whether our standard Managed Services agreement covers the attestation language Mina mentioned and, if not, share suggested contract language by EOD Monday.

Thanks everyone — will attach the control-mapping-draft.xlsx and the evidence-retention-summary.pdf to the package we send to Acme's intake team.

—Grace
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
